items.title: Agent de la DGSE libéré : le Maroc, médiateur clé au Mali
items.description: La grâce accordée par le président malien Assimi Goïta à un agent français détenu depuis près d’un an intervient au terme de plusieurs mois de tractations diplomatiques. Selon Le Monde, le Maroc a joué un rôle dans les discussions ayant conduit à cette libération, confirmant la place singulière de Rabat comme interlocuteur fiable entre Paris et Bamako. La libération de Yann Vézilier met en lumière la capacité du Maroc à intervenir dans les dossiers les plus sensibles entre la France et les pays du Sahel, en s’appuyant sur des relations politiques et sécuritaires construites de longue date avec les capitales de la région. Détenu au Mali depuis août 2025, l’agent de la Direction générale de la sécurité extérieure (DGSE) avait été condamné, le 5 juin, à vingt ans de prison pour atteinte à la sûreté de l’État. Les autorités maliennes lui reprochaient notamment sa participation à une tentative de déstabilisation du pays. Le 13 août, Assimi Goïta lui a finalement accordé une grâce présidentielle, ouvrant la voie à son départ du territoire malien. Le Maroc au cœur des tractations C’est dans les tractations ayant précédé cette décision que le rôle de Rabat apparaît. Le Monde rapporte que le gouvernement malien a remercié, dans son communiqué, un « pays frère » pour ses « bons offices ». Citant une source militaire malienne, le quotidien français identifie le Maroc comme l’acteur ayant joué un rôle dans les discussions ayant abouti à la libération de l’agent français. Cette mention prend une dimension particulière au regard des relations entre Rabat et Bamako. Le Maroc a fait le choix de maintenir et de renforcer ses liens avec les pays du Sahel, y compris dans une période de profondes recompositions politiques et diplomatiques. Cette politique lui a permis de préserver des canaux de communication directs avec les autorités maliennes. Le précédent burkinabè Ce dossier rappelle surtout une opération similaire menée au Burkina Faso. En décembre 2024, quatre agents de la DGSE détenus à Ouagadougou avaient été libérés grâce à une médiation marocaine. Le Monde avait alors consacré plusieurs articles à cette opération et décrit précisément le rôle joué par Rabat. Selon le quotidien français, plusieurs démarches avaient échoué avant que les autorités françaises ne se tournent vers le Maroc. Rabat disposait alors de relais solides au Burkina Faso, notamment grâce aux relations développées de longue date entre les deux pays et à la coopération entre leurs appareils sécuritaires. Le Monde avait notamment révélé que des responsables burkinabè avaient été formés au Maroc et que certains interlocuteurs sécuritaires des deux pays entretenaient des relations personnelles. Ces réseaux ont permis à Rabat d’établir un canal de discussion efficace au moment où les relations entre Paris et Ouagadougou étaient fortement dégradées. Une relation privilégiée avec Bamako Depuis longtemps, Rabat a développé une relation étroite avec Bamako, fondée sur des liens politiques, économiques, religieux et sécuritaires. Cette proximité constitue aujourd’hui un capital diplomatique particulièrement précieux. C’est précisément cette relation qui permet au Maroc d’intervenir dans des dossiers où la confiance constitue la principale condition du succès. Dans l’affaire Vézilier, Bamako a choisi de reconnaître les « bons offices » d’un « pays frère ». Le choix des mots du gouvernement malien n’est pas anodin. Il traduit la nature particulière de la relation entre les deux pays et le niveau de confiance dont bénéficie Rabat auprès des autorités maliennes. The post Agent de la DGSE libéré : le Maroc, médiateur clé au Mali appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Jason Arday, ex-Cambridge professor accused of plagiarism, found dead
items.description: Black academic Jason Arday, who resigned from the University of Cambridge last week following a high-profile plagiarism scandal that raised claims of racism, was found dead Friday, the prestigious British institution confirmed. Arday, 41, was found unresponsive Friday afternoon at an address in south London, according to the capital’s Metropolitan Police Service, which did not confirm the identity of the deceased person at the time of discovery. “We are desperately saddened to hear this tragic news,” Cambridge University’s top administrator, Vice-Chancellor Deborah Prentice, said in a brief statement. Arday’s family criticised what they called a “campaign of harassment” that followed allegations about his academic work and personal life. “The campaign of misinformation was too much for Jason, who was a gentle man and who always wanted to see the best in everyone,” the family said in a statement released through his publisher Simon & Schuster. The scandal erupted after some academics and media reports accused Arday, who became Cambridge’s youngest black professor in 2023, of plagiarising parts of his doctoral thesis. The allegations have been seized on by British right-wing newspapers and commentators, who claim that he unfairly benefited from diversity, equality and inclusion (DEI) policies. Arday announced on August 5 that he was resigning from both his university post as a professor and as a fellow of Jesus College, shortly after they announced probes into the various accusations. In a letter posted online, Arday said that quitting was “the only way” to end a “difficult period”, but insisted the decision should not be “mistaken for an acceptance of the narratives that have surrounded me”. – Newspaper claims – Police said officers had been called by the London Ambulance Service “following a report that a man had been found unresponsive inside a property” in the city’s Battersea neighbourhood. “Sadly, a 41-year-old man was pronounced dead at the scene,” it said in a statement, noting his next-of-kin had been informed. “At this time his death is being treated as unexpected, but is not believed to be suspicious. “The case is being investigated by officers from the Met’s Central South Command Unit. A file will be prepared for the coroner.” Education Secretary Lucy Powell said she was “deeply shocked (and) saddened” by the news. She urged people to give his family “privacy through this incredibly difficult period (and) to remember there are real people with loved ones involved”. The furore around Arday grew after Nathan Cofnas, a US academic and self-defined “race realist” — whose Cambridge research affiliation ended in 2024 amid racism accusations — published claims about him in July. The allegations included that multiple sections of Arday’s doctoral dissertation were copied from other works. The Times and Telegraph newspapers have published several investigative articles into Arday’s academic work and personal life. Some of his claims about his personal life, including that he once ran 30 marathons in 35 days and raised millions for charities, were also disputed. – ‘Racially motivated’ – In an interview with The Times earlier this month, Arday admitted making academic “mistakes” but said he was being wrongly “portrayed to be a liar and a fantasist and an academic fraud”. He also alleged the “campaign to unseat me from my position” was “racially motivated”. The controversy around Arday appears to have divided the Cambridge campus and wider academia. A group of university academics last week wrote to Prentice slamming Arday’s appointment and asking her to appoint an independent body to probe what happened. Others have written joint letters in support of him. On Wednesday, Prentice had called his alleged wrongdoing “an aberration” and vowed a thorough and transparent investigation, while insisting it should not be used “to cast aspersions” on other academics from ethnic minority backgrounds. The American psychologist promised the probe would look into the “circumstances” of Arday’s appointment and his time in post that would include academics from “beyond Cambridge”. Arday’s memoir — “Great and Unfortunate Things” — had been published in the United States the previous day, ahead of its planned release in Britain later this month. It has also attracted scrutiny. AFP The post Jason Arday, ex-Cambridge professor accused of plagiarism, found dead appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Le Cap-Vert, la Leçon des Petites Nations (Dr.Pierrette Herzberger-Fofana)
items.description: Quand le football change le regard du monde L a Coupe du monde 2026 restera comme celle où une petite nation insulaire de moins de 600 000 habitants a obligé le monde à revoir ses certitudes. Elle rappelle que, dans le concert des nations, la grandeur ne dépend ni du territoire ni de la population. Les Tubarões Azuis (les Requins Bleus) ont été l’une des plus belles surprises de ce Mondial. Une victoire qui dépasse le sport Le Cap-Vert n'a pas remporté le trophée. Pourtant, il est devenu l'une des grandes révélations du tournoi. Les Tubarões Azuis (Les Requins Bleus) ont démontré qu'en football comme dans la vie, la grandeur ne se mesure ni à la superficie d'un territoire, ni au poids démographique d'un pays. Les Requins Bleus ont conquis le cœur de millions de supporters à travers le monde. L’équipe nationale du Cap-Vert est entrée de plain-pied dans l’histoire du football universel. Elle quitte la compétition la tête haute et retourne au pays fière de ses exploits sportifs. Pendant quelques semaines, cet archipel de l’Atlantique est devenu le cœur battant d’une émotion mondiale. II.La légende de la Genèse du Cap-Vert Selon la légende, Le Bon Dieu aurait créé ces dix îles au large du Sénégal une fois qu’il eut terminé son œuvre de création ou genèse. Le Tout-Puissant aurait secoué Ses mains au-dessus de l’Atlantique. De la mer aurait jailli ces dix îles qui symbolisent que l’Homme doit gagner son pain à la sueur de son front. Cette légende sur l’origine du Cap-Vert que ma mère m’ a souvent racontée, a bercé mon enfance. Les 10 îles du Cap-Vert (carte du Cap-Vert) Elle a été transmise de génération en génération, dans la famille, et ne figure dans aucun ouvrage. J’aime croire à cette légende qui a émerveillé mon enfance, comme j’aime me souvenir des ladainhas , ces veillées de prières, de chants, de récits, de festivités et d’incantations mystiques et poétiques à la louange des saints et des grandes figures du pays. Tout comme je me souviens des séances de chants et de danse ” le battuku ”, lors des cérémonies de mariage, dans lequel un morceau de tissu sert d'instrument de percussion, animé par une chanteuse et des choristes. Les paroles abordent souvent la critique sociale, le quotidien ou des faits historiques. L’archipel offre un paysage volcanique très accidenté. Ces dix îles qui semblent défier vents et océans, sont situées entre l’Europe, l’Amérique et l’Afrique. Elles baignent dans l'océan Atlantique, à environ 450 km au large du continent africain. Les îles, dont neuf sont habitées, se différencient selon leur orientation au vent. Au Nord, le groupe de Barlavento “au delà du vent”, englobe les îles de Boa Vista, Sal, São Nicolau, Santo Antão, et São Vicente. Au sud, le groupe Sotavento “sous le vent”, comprend les îles de Brava, Fogo, Santiago qui est la plus grande et la plus peuplée, et Maiao. ”. Ces dix îles de rêve ont chacune leur spécificité. Ainsi, Sal, est l’île ensoleillée, Boa Vista, l’île au climat agréable, où il fait bon vivre. Brava, l’île aux fleurs; Santiago, l’île fertile. São Vicente reflète le cœur de la musique capverdienne. La richesse de sa musique aux sons des “ mornas ”, des “ coladeira ” et du “ funana ” ont traversé les océans grâce à la diva aux pieds nus, Cesaria Evora qui caractérise l’âme capverdienne. L’histoire du Cap-Vert explique aussi ce destin singulier. Situé au carrefour de l’Europe, de l’Afrique et des Amériques, l’archipel fut pendant des siècles un point de rencontre des routes maritimes, mais aussi de la Traite transatlantique. Des épreuves, des sécheresses, des famines et de l’émigration est née une nation qui a appris à transformer la résilience en force collective. III.Le triomphe d'une diaspora active Le Cap-Vert possède peut-être la diaspora la plus transnationale d'Afrique. Les Capverdiens sont un peuple de migrants. On constate un fait unique dans l’histoire, il y a plus de Capverdiens et des descendants de Capverdiens qui vivent à l’étranger que dans le pays même, au total, environ 700 000. Ils ont émigré notamment aux USA, dans le New England, à Boston, New Bedford, en Europe au Portugal, au Brésil, en France,aux Pays-Bas, au Luxembourg et en Belgique et dans les pays lusophones mais aussi dans les pays voisins comme le Sénégal. La ville de Pawtucket aux Etats-Unis par exemple compte la plus grande communauté capverdienne. La plupart des associations capverdiennes à travers le monde se font un devoir de transmettre leur culture sous diverses facettes. Pawtucket, dans le Rhode Island, abrite par exemple l'une des plus grandes et dynamiques communautés capverdiennes des États-Unis. La ville propose un riche patrimoine culturel. Chaque année, la rue se transforme en un festival à ciel ouvert dédié au cachupa (plat national) L'attraction principale est le concours du meilleur cachupa entre plusieurs restaurants locaux, accompagné de spectacles de danse traditionnelle, de concerts et de chants. Au Pays-Bas, on compte en tout 37 000 Capverdiens, en Angola 35 000, au Brésil 20 000 et au Sénégal 20 000. La diaspora cap-verdienne entretient un lien culturel extrêmement fort avec la terre d’origine. Cette ferveur s’est exprimée avec une intensité particulière durant les matchs des Requins Bleus. Une leçon pour le monde Le parcours capverdien rappelle qu'il existe une autre manière d'être une puissance. Le Cap-Vert ne possède ni une immense armée, ni d'immenses richesses naturelles. Son influence repose d'abord sur la stabilité démocratique qui demeure depuis son indépendance le 5 juillet 1975. Le Cap-Vert est l'un des pays les plus stables, démocratiques et pacifiques d'Afrique, caractérisé par des alternances régulières au pouvoir, le respect de l'État de droit et une absence totale de conflits armés ou de tensions internes majeures. Cette stabilité repose également sur une Démocratie enracinée dans le partage du pouvoir: Le multipartisme fonctionne sans heurts depuis 1990, avec des scrutins libres, transparents et acceptés par tous les camps. Climat social apaisé: Le pays ne connaît pas de menaces terroristes ni de violences politiques notables, garantissant une paix civile durable. La vie politique se concentre principalement sur des défis d'ordre climatique et économique, comme la gestion de la rareté de l'eau, la dépendance au tourisme et la cherté de la vie, la sécheresse. Le problème de l’eau ou plutôt du manque d’eau est à l’origine de l’émigration. Le soutien financier important de sa diaspora à l'étranger contribue aussi à la stabilité économique du pays. Sécurité maritime: La pêche maritime est le socle de l’économie. L'insularité de l'archipel en fait un point de passage exposé aux trafics internationaux de stupéfiants, géré par une coopération policière active avec les partenaires internationaux. Mais surtout sur l’éducation sur la valeur et le sens du travail bien fait jouent un rôle primordial et méritent une attention particulière. Pour le Capverdien, le travail fait partie de sa personnalité. C’est une valeur que les parents inculquent aux enfants dès le bas-âge. D’ailleurs nombreuses sont les femmes capverdiennes d’un certain âge qui racontent comment elles ont travaillé dur toute leur vie pour élever leurs enfants suite à l’émigration du père, à la recherche d’un emploi. Certaines d’entre elles refusent même de divulguer leurs secrets culinaires, tellement elles sont fières du label de cordons bleus qui restent attaché à leurs noms. Les nombreux proverbes qui parsèment leur langage mettent l’emphase sur l’amour du travail bien fait. Ainsi, généralement, les Capverdiens vivent selon le principe voulant que : “ ce qui est excellent est tout juste bon pour moi. Je ne peux donc exiger pour mon travail rien de moins que ce qui est excellent”. L’éducation, associée à une diaspora active, a contribué à diffuser la culture capverdienne bien au-delà des îles.Il en est de même des associations capverdiennes à travers le monde qui transmettent une culture universelle portée par la voix de Césaria Evora, la diva de la chanson capverdienne. 75% de la population est alphabétisée. Le créole capverdien ( crioulo ) est la langue maternelle de la population, tandis que le portugais est la langue de l’administration et de l’enseignement formel. Grâce à sa musique, Cesária Évora a fait découvrir à des millions de personnes la morna , ces chansons douces et mélancoliques qui expriment l’âme d’une nation . Sa célèbre chanson «Sodade» est devenue un emblème de la musique capverdienne et de la nostalgie ressentie par des générations marquées par le départ et la migration. La morna pourrait être considérée comme le blues traditionnel du Cap-Vert et et Cesária Évora en était la reine incontestée. Des chansons telles que «Petit Pays », «Sangue de Beirona » et « Angola» véhiculent différents aspects de l’histoire, de la mémoire et de l’identité capverdienne au-delà des frontières linguistiques et nationales. “ Petit Pays “ est une déclaration d'amour mélancolique à son île natale, chantée en créole et en français. “ Sangue de Beirona ” : Un morceau rythmé et entraînant, représentatif du genre coladeira . “Angola ” : Un titre puissant devenu un classique de ses concerts et qui évoque le thème de l’émigration. Le Cap-Vert, quant à lui, a rendu hommage à Cesária Évora en plaçant son portrait sur son billet de 2 000 escudos. Bien avant que le football ne fasse connaître les îles à un nouveau public mondial, la musique avait déjà fait voyager le Cap-Vert à travers le monde. V.L'héritage Amilcar Cabral (12 septembre 1924 – 20 janvier 1973) On ne peut raconter l’histoire du Cap-Vert sans évoquer Amílcar Cabral, l’un des plus grands penseurs et leaders de la lutte pour la libération de la Guinée-Bissau et du Cap-Vert. Né de parents Capverdiens en Guinée-Bissau à Bafatá alors colonie portugaise, le jeune Amílcar Cabral part en 1945 au Portugal pour y étudier l’agronomie.Il créé avec d’autres camarades le PAIG aujourd’hui PAICV. Assassiné environ huit mois avant la déclaration unilatérale d'indépendance de la Guinée-Bissau et du Cap-Vert, à Conakry, Cabral ne verra pas son rêve se réaliser la libération du joug colonial de ces deux patries. Sa vision de la liberté, de la dignité et de l’éducation a inspiré non seulement l’indépendance de la Guinée-Bissau et du Cap-Vert, mais aussi des générations d’Africains à travers le monde. En honneur de ce héros de la liberté, j’ai donné son nom à l’un de mes fils. Grâce aux Tubarões Azuis ,(Requins Bleus) je n’ai plus besoin d’expliquer la signification de ce prénom, ni où se trouve le Cap-Vert. Le plus grand Aéroport international du Cap-Vert (SID) à Sal porte son nom. Le football a rendu visible ce que beaucoup ignoraient déjà. Si le football a révélé le Cap-Vert au monde, cette réussite n’est pas le fruit du hasard. Elle s’ enracine dans une histoire, une culture et une conception de la liberté qui ont façonné le pays depuis des générations. Héritage personnel Je suis née à Bamako, j'ai grandi à Dakar. Mon père est originaire de Guinée (Conakry) et ma mère du Cap-Vert. Par ma Maman , je suis la petite-fille de Ñhu Nacu, l'une des figures historiques les plus respectées du Cap-Vert, dont la vie incarne les valeurs de courage, de dévouement à la chose publique et d'engagement envers son peuple. C'est pourquoi cette aventure des Tubarões Azuis (Les Requins bleus) dépasse pour moi le simple football. Chaque victoire réveillait le souvenir de ma mère, de mon enfance et de ces îles qui continuent d'habiter ma mémoire. J'aurais tant aimé que ma Maman puisse voir ce moment où le monde entier applaudissait enfin le pays qu'elle aimait tant. VII. La Victoire des Petites Nations Les Capverdiens, les Capverdiennes sont un peuple chaleureux dont la musique langoureuse et nostalgique évoque l’histoire de l’archipel. Leur présence au Mondial a été saluée et appréciée par le monde entier. Ils ont donné un autre visage du continent. Le Cap-Vert n'a peut-être pas remporté la Coupe du monde. Mais il a gagné quelque chose qui ne figure dans aucun classement FIFA : le respect et l'admiration de millions de personnes. Dans une époque où l'on confond souvent puissance et grandeur, les Tubarões Azuis nous rappellent qu'un petit pays peut changer le regard de l’autre, lorsqu'il révèle au monde le talent, la résilience et la force d'une petite nation. Leur parcours restera comme la victoire de toutes les petites Nations qui refusent d'être condamnées à l'invisibilité. Dr.Pierrette Herzberger-Fofana Citoyenne d'honneur d'Erlangen.Allemagne Ancienne Députée au Parlement Européen L’article Le Cap-Vert, la Leçon des Petites Nations (Dr.Pierrette Herzberger-Fofana) est apparu en premier sur Mediaguinee.com .

items.title: Maroc | Projet de dessalement de l’eau de mer de 410 millions de m³/an
items.description: Le gouvernement marocain a autorisé la société OCP Green Water, filiale du Groupe OCP, à créer deux nouvelles sociétés spécialisées dans le dessalement de l’eau de mer et son transport, dans le cadre d’un projet dont la capacité globale atteindra 410 millions de mètres cubes par an. A comparer avec les 92 millions de mètres cubes de capacité annuelle globale des quatre stations de dessalement tunisiennes basées à Djerba, Gabès Sfax et Sousse. A comparer aussi avec les 5 500 millions de mètres cubes produits actuellement par l’Arabie saoudite, premier producteur mondial d'eau dessalée, assurant à lui seul 20 % à 22 % du volume total d’eau dessalée dans le monde. Habib Glenza , à Lodz. Cette initiative s’inscrit dans les efforts visant à développer de nouvelles ressources en eau face aux défis croissants liés au stress hydrique et à renforcer la souveraineté hydrique du Royaume. L’autorisation est prévue par le décret n° 2.26.547, publié au Bulletin officiel n° 7531 du 3 août 2026. Signé le 23 juillet 2026 (8 Safar 1448), le texte permet à OCP Green Water de mettre en place deux entités distinctes dédiées aux activités de dessalement de l’eau de mer et son transport. Cette opération s’inscrit dans la stratégie du Groupe OCP, actif dans le domaine d l’extraction et de la transformation du phosphate, visant à couvrir l’intégralité de ses besoins industriels en eau à travers le développement de ressources hydriques non conventionnelles. Elle répond également à une ambition plus large consistant à contribuer à la souveraineté hydrique nationale en mettant à disposition de l’eau destinée aux usages industriels, à la consommation humaine et à l’irrigation agricole. Deux sociétés vont gérer les structures de dessalement. La première couvrira la zone centrale, comprenant les provinces et villes de Safi, Benguerir, Youssoufia et Marrakech. Sa capacité de production est fixée à 195 millions de mètres cubes d’eau dessalée par an. La seconde interviendra dans la zone nord, qui englobe Jorf Lasfar, El Jadida, Casablanca et Khouribga. Elle disposera d’une capacité annuelle de 215 millions de mètres cubes. Les deux structures en question, devraient donc produire 410 millions de mètres cubes d’eau dessalée chaque année, un volume appelé à renforcer significativement l’offre hydrique dans plusieurs régions stratégiques du pays. Le décret précise que l’eau produite ne sera pas exclusivement destinée aux activités du Groupe OCP. Une partie de cette ressource devra également contribuer à l’alimentation en eau potable des populations des territoires concernés ainsi qu’à l’irrigation des périmètres agricoles. Les deux sociétés auront pour mission d’assurer la production et la distribution de l’eau dessalée au profit des usagers urbains, industriels et agricoles. Elles s’appuieront sur des infrastructures modernes intégrant les énergies renouvelables, dans une logique de durabilité et d’optimisation des ressources. Au-delà de l’augmentation des capacités de dessalement, le projet vise aussi à restructurer les actifs liés au dessalement et au transport de l’eau au sein d’entités spécialisées et autonomes. L’opération s’inscrit, selon le décret, dans les orientations de la politique actionnariale de l’État, notamment en matière de renforcement de la souveraineté hydrique, de développement des partenariats public-privé dans les infrastructures et de meilleure coordination des projets portés par les organismes publics. L’autorisation gouvernementale est intervenue après consultation de l’Agence nationale de gestion stratégique des participations de l’État et de suivi de la performance des établissements et entreprises publics, sur proposition de la ministre de l’Économie et des Finances. Le décret prévoit enfin que l’autorisation accordée demeure valable pendant une année à compter de sa publication au Bulletin officiel. Rédigé à Rabat le 23 juillet 2026, le texte est signé par le chef du gouvernement, Aziz Akhannouch, et contresigné par la ministre de l’Économie et des Finances, Nadia Fettah. Avec cette décision, les autorités marocaines dotent OCP Green Water du cadre juridique nécessaire à la création de deux sociétés spécialisées dans le dessalement et le transport de l’eau de mer. L’objectif affiché est de mobiliser une capacité annuelle de 410 millions de mètres cubes, destinée à répondre aux besoins industriels, urbains et agricoles, tout en contribuant au renforcement de la sécurité et de la souveraineté hydriques du Royaume. items.title: Port de Tanger: Hausse de 98% des débarquements de pêche à fin juillet
items.description: Les débarquements de la pêche côtière et artisanale au niveau du port de Tanger ont atteint 5.239 tonnes (T) à fin juillet 2026, en hausse de 98% par rapport à la même période de l'année précédente, selon l'Office national des pêches (ONP). La valeur marchande de ces captures a progressé de 14% à 146,15 millions de dirhams (MDH) à fin juillet dernier, contre plus de 128,70 MDH à fin juillet 2025, a précisé l'ONP dans son dernier rapport sur les statistiques de la pêche côtière et artisanale au Maroc. Par espèce, les quantités de poissons pélagiques débarquées dans ce port ont progressé de 111% au cours des sept premiers mois de cette année à 3.630 T, pour une valeur estimée à 74,39 MDH (+18%), contre environ 62,97 DH/1.722 T à fin juillet 2025. Les débarquements des poissons blancs se sont, quant à eux, accrus de 125% à 999 T, pour une valeur de plus de 35,17 MDH (+35%), contre environ 25,99 MDH/ 444 T une année auparavant. S'agissant des débarquements des céphalopodes, ils ont augmenté de 32% à 440 T pour des recettes de plus de 27,42 MDH (-7%), tandis que pour les crustacés, les débarquements ont augmenté de 11% à 169 T, générant des revenus de plus de 9,16 MDH (-12%). Au niveau national, les débarquements des produits commercialisés de la pêche côtière et artisanale se sont établis à 551.547 T à fin juillet dernier, en hausse de 5% par rapport à la même période de l'année précédente. En valeur, ces débarquements ont augmenté de 2% à plus de 6,28 milliards de dirhams (MMDH) contre 6,15 MMDH en glissement annuel. items.title: Armed personnel have surrounded Osun Speaker’s residence – Adeleke camp
items.description: The Adeleke Campaign Council has raised the alarm over the alleged deployment of armed security personnel to the residence of the Speaker of the Osun State House of Assembly, Adewale Egbedun, on Saturday as the state holds its governorship election. The campaign council, in a statement issued by its spokesperson, Pelumi Olajengbesi, alleged that the security personnel arrived at the Speaker’s residence in more than 10 black Hilux vehicles and subsequently surrounded the premises. According to the council, the residence was effectively sealed off, with people inside allegedly prevented from leaving. However, the campaign council said it was unable to independently establish the purpose of the deployment or determine whether the personnel were providing security or acting in an official capacity. “We have received reports that the residence of the Speaker of the Osun State House of Assembly, Rt. Hon. Adewale Egbedun, has been surrounded by armed security personnel who reportedly arrived in more than 10 black Hilux vehicles,” the statement said. “We have also been informed that the residence has effectively been sealed off, with everyone inside reportedly prevented from leaving the premises.” The council called on the relevant security authorities to immediately explain the reason for the reported deployment and restriction of movement around the Speaker’s residence. Olajengbesi said efforts to contact the Commissioner of Police responsible for election security in Osun State and the Deputy Inspector-General of Police overseeing the election were unsuccessful. He also said attempts to reach the Police Situation Room were unsuccessful, adding that the publicly provided telephone number was switched off. The campaign council urged security agencies to conduct their operations in a manner that would not create fear or intimidation among residents on election day. “On this Election Day, the people of Osun State deserve an atmosphere free from fear and intimidation. Security deployments must inspire confidence and protect the integrity of the electoral process,” it said. The council further appealed to residents to remain calm and law-abiding while awaiting clarification from the security authorities. “The people of Osun State must be allowed to come out peacefully and decide their future according to their own conscience, without intimidation or interference,” the statement added. The post Armed personnel have surrounded Osun Speaker’s residence – Adeleke camp appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Powerful quake off Indonesia kills 20, sparks mass evacuations
items.description: Rescuers combed through debris for survivors on Saturday after a powerful earthquake struck off Flores island in eastern Indonesia, killing at least 20 people and sending thousands fleeing. As the full scale of the disaster unfolded, rescue official Fathur Rahman told AFP at least 20 people were confirmed dead from four different towns on the island, popular with tourists. “From the reports we have received, 20 people have died, six are injured, and two are still buried,” Fathur said by telephone from a boat on his way to Nagekeo regency, the hardest-hit area. Two people were known to be trapped alive under rubble in the neighbouring Manggarai regency after the 7.7-magnitude jolt. “Our focus will be on locating the victims who are buried under the rubble” said Fathur, adding the rescue effort had been complicated by landslides cutting off several roads. Residents in Nagekeo, the area closest to the epicentre, raced for higher ground as the sea retreated earlier Saturday — a possible sign of an approaching tsunami, AFP journalists witnessed. A tsunami warning was later lifted but people were warned not to return to damaged buildings for fear that aftershocks may bring them down. Dozens of aftershocks have already been felt, the strongest measured at a magnitude of 6.1. ‘My family is safe’ Yohanes Babo, 56, a resident of Nagekeo, said he was at a market when the earth started shaking in the early morning hours. “The shaking was strong. Thankfully, we were already outside the house,” he told AFP . “People were panicking, running here and there. We’re evacuating for the time being … and trying to get to the hills,” he said, adding: “My family is safe. No one was harmed.” The epicentre of the shallow quake was located just off the north coast of the island, about 68 kilometres (42 miles) northwest of the coastal town of Ende, US and Indonesian authorities said. Rescuers pull one dead body from the rubble of a building that partly collapsed at the port of Maumere. Fathur said two people were evacuated alive from the debris and “one was found deceased”, according to video footage released by the agency. The full extent of the damage is still being assessed. Lukas Lotar, a resident of Maumere about 2,500 kilometres (1,553 miles) east of Jakarta, recounted how the earth “suddenly started to shake and I panicked”. “Patients also fled the hospital, the jolt was big. I saw some walls were cracked,” Lotar, a hospital customer service official told AFP . The stricken area is comprised mostly of towns and villages with few, if any, high-rise buildings. Monitoring sea level Indonesia’s Meteorology, Climatology, and Geophysics Agency (BMKG) initially warned of possible tsunami waves following the quake and urged people to get to higher ground. Long queues of people could be seen evacuating towns on foot, by motorbike and car, some piled into the back of pickup trucks. “We have ended (the tsunami warning) but we will keep monitoring the sea level,” said BMKG earthquake and tsunami director Wijayanto, who like many Indonesians goes by one name. Indonesia and neighbouring countries experience frequent earthquakes due to their location in the Pacific “Ring of Fire” — an arc of intense seismic activity stretching from Japan through Southeast Asia and across the Pacific basin. Flores was struck by a 7.7-magnitude earthquake in 1992, which triggered a tsunami and resulted in around 2,500 deaths. Among Indonesia’s history of deadly quakes is a devastating 9.1-magnitude tremor in 2004 that struck off the coast of Sumatra and triggered a tsunami that killed 220,000 throughout the region, about 170,000 of them in Indonesia. The Boxing Day tragedy was one of the deadliest natural disasters in recorded history. In 2018, a powerful quake shook the island of Lombok and several more tremors followed over the next couple of weeks, killing more than 550 people on the holiday island and neighbouring Sumbawa. Later that year, a 7.5-magnitude quake and a subsequent tsunami in Palu on Sulawesi island left more than 4,300 people dead or missing.

items.title: PM Shehbaz directs NDMA to ensure relief for citizens in flood-hit areas
items.description: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Saturday directed the National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA) to provide every possible assistance and relief to people in flood-affected areas. According to a statement issued by the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO), the prime minister gave the directives during a meeting with NDMA Chairman Lieutenant General Inam Haider Malik. The prime minister directed that “all available resources should be utilised to provide every possible assistance and relief to the people in flood-affected areas”. He further instructed the NDMA to maintain effective coordination with relevant provincial institutions and Provincial Disaster Management Authorities (PDMAs). The prime minister also appreciated the use of artificial intelligence and modern technology at the National Emergencies Operation Centre. During the meeting, the NDMA chairman briefed the prime minister on the country’s weather situation, particularly the flood situation in the wake of monsoon rains. The chairman also briefed the prime minister on relief activities in flood-affected areas and measures being taken for the rehabilitation of flood victims. With the cooperation of the federal government, NDMA relief operations in flood-affected areas of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KP), Gilgit-Baltistan (GB) and Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK) will continue, the statement quoted the chairman as saying. According to the NDMA , 155 people have lost their lives and 460 have been injured in rain-related incidents from June 26 to August 14. Monsoon rains fall across the region from June to September, offering respite from the summer heat and are crucial to replenishing water supplies. However, heavy downpours also trigger deadly floods, landslides and displacement, particularly in vulnerable, poorly drained, or densely populated areas. On Friday, the Flood Forecasting Division of the Pakistan Meteorological Department warned of possible high flooding in storm-water nullahs linked to the Chenab and Ravi rivers from Aug 15 to 21 as flows in these waterways continue to rise.

items.title: World Cup, Super Eagles’ AFCON heartbreak, others dominate Google searches
items.description: By Juliet Umeh THE FIFA World Cup, the Super Eagles’ Africa Cup of Nations, AFCON, heartbreak, the Blord-VDM saga and the mysterious “67” Gen Z meme were among the stories that scenic Nigerians rushing to Google in the first seven months of 2026. Fresh Google Trends data covering January to July 2026 showed that Nigerians turned to the search engine to understand major sporting events, geopolitical tensions, celebrity controversies, deaths, internet culture and developments affecting their everyday lives. “Every big story now has a second life in the search bar,” Google said in its review of the trends. “When the Super Eagles lost a semi-final on penalties, when a strait most people had never thought about pushed up the price of petrol, when a music promoter’s car crash reopened a three-year-old argument, Nigerians went to Google.” According to the data, the FIFA World Cup emerged as the biggest search story of the period, generating interest several times higher than other major topics. Nigerians followed the tournament closely, searching for information on the Super Eagles’ campaign, the opening ceremony featuring Burna Boy and Shakira, major matches and the eventual final. “The World Cup over everything,” Google said, noting that “no story came close.” The Africa Cup of Nations also dominated searches in January, particularly after Nigeria’s semi-final defeat to Morocco on penalties. “January belonged to AFCON, and to heartbreak,” Google said, adding that “Nigeria vs Morocco” became one of the biggest individual queries of 2026. The search record, according to Google, showed “a country going through the full arc: fixtures, hope, heartbreak, and ‘AFCON final’ anyway.” February produced another surprise, as the Milan-Cortina Winter Olympics attracted significant search interest among Nigerians, including searches around ice hockey and other winter sports. “Nigeria watched a Winter Olympics,” Google said. The company added: “Curiosity, it turns out, does not need snow.” Beyond sports, developments involving Iran and the Strait of Hormuz also drove significant searches, highlighting how international events could quickly become local concerns. Queries including “Iran news”, “Israel Iran war” and “strait of hormuz meaning” spiked as tensions around the strategic waterway raised concerns about global oil supplies and prices. “Geopolitics rarely trends in the abstract,” Google said. It explained that when tensions around the Strait of Hormuz intensified, Nigerians searched for both the international developments and their implications. “A war three thousand miles away was also a story about the cost of the ride to work,” Google said. The controversy involving cryptocurrency entrepreneur Blord and social media activist VeryDarkMan was another major search driver. items.title: Outrage grows as stakeholders raise airport security, safety concerns over picketing of Air Peace
items.description: By Dickson Omobola The decision of aviation unions to picket Nigeria’s largest airline, Air Peace, Tuesday, has elicited sharp criticism from stakeholders in the country’s air transport sector, with many saying the action constituted serious safety and security concerns. From the early hours of Tuesday until about noon, members of the National Union of Air Transport Employees, NUATE, and the Air Transport Services Senior Staff Association of Nigeria, ATSSSAN, backed by the Nigeria Labour Congress, NLC, and the Trade Union Congress, TUC, disrupted Air Peace’s operations over the alleged non-remittance of the five per cent Ticket Sales Charge, TSC, to the Nigeria Civil Aviation Authority, NCAA, and the right of workers to unionise. The industrial action followed a series of ultimatums the unions said they issued to the Airline Operators of Nigeria, AON. The latest came on August 7, when the unions gave airlines a three day notice, threatening to picket operators that failed to remit the statutory five per cent TSC to the NCAA and allow their staff to join aviation unions. Acting on the threat, union members converged on the domestic terminals of the Murtala Muhammed Airport, Lagos, and the Nnamdi Azikiwe International Airport, Abuja, where they singled out Air Peace, blocked access to its counters and prevented the airline’s scheduled flights from departing until the Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Mr Festus Keyamo, intervened. The action, which disrupted more than half of the airline’s operations that day, left thousands of passengers stranded and caused the airline to lose more than N2 billion in revenue. Memories The incident, which sparked debate over the implications of industrial disputes for aviation safety, airport security and passenger confidence, revived memories of previous occasions when labour disputes led to the disruption of airline operations, exposing travellers to the fallout. Over a decade ago, precisely March 13, 2013, members of NUATE and ATSSSAN grounded Aero Contractors’ operations over allegations of poor staff welfare and anti-union practices. The action stranded more than 100 passengers at the Domestic Terminal of the Murtala Muhammed Airport 2, MMA2, in Lagos. On March 23, 2017, aviation unions also grounded Arik Air’s operations at the General Aviation Terminal, GAT, of the Murtala Muhammed Airport, Lagos. Three years later, specifically on September 13, 2020, NUATE and ATSSSAN again disrupted Arik Air’s operations by barricading the entrance to the airline’s operational headquarters in Lagos over unresolved labour issues. Passengers lament However, passengers caught in the disruption that happened on Tuesday were left to grapple with missed appointments and what could be an unexpected financial loss. Speaking to Saturday Vanguard, a passenger who simply identified himself as Chinedu said: “I had a flight for 7:00 am. My mum fell sick last night (Monday) and she was rushed to the hospital. I had hoped that I would get to Abuja early today so that I could look after her, as my siblings are not there to do so.” Kitty Kat, who took to X to express her frustration, said: “I received a flight reminder at 2 am both via text and email only to arrive at the airport and encounter this development. No proper information, no communication from the airline. We’re just being told that no Air Peace aircraft is leaving the airport today, regardless of your destination. Honestly, this is beyond frustration. You plan, you prepare, you get to the airport on time, and then this happens with zero explanation.” Experts’ views Commenting on the issue, former commandant of the Murtala Mohammed International Airport, Lagos, Group Captain John Ojikutu, retd, described the unions’ action as unlawful. Ojikutu, in a chat with Saturday Vanguard, also called for regulations prohibiting acts of unlawful interference with aviation activities at airports. He said: “As far as I am concerned, there is a regulatory authority in aviation and that is the NCAA. Aviation is governed by international law. That is why I said it is the negligence of the NCAA that resulted in the action. The NCAA should produce a law that removes acts of unlawful interference in the activities of aviation in the airport. Or put it as a guideline for the Federal Airports Authority of Nigeria, FAAN. “If they (the unions) have to picket the airline, let them go to the airline’s office, not the airport. The airline has an office outside the airport. They should go there and protest there. The picketing did not affect only Air Peace; it also affected others. It has a negative effect on this country. I am surprised that the NCAA is not treating this as its responsibility. “Suppose there were people who had infiltrated them (the unions). I am also surprised that the DSS was there and did not look into it. What is aviation? Aviation is a national security asset. Contempt For former Acting Director-General/Managing Director of the NCAA, Engr Benedict Adeyileka, the unions acted in contempt of court because there was a subsisting judgment of the Federal High Court on Air Peace and the unions. Speaking to Saturday Vanguard, Adeyileka said: “From a neutral and a regulatory point of view: the minister, to the best of my knowledge, had intervened in the issue. They were all still in the process of talking about strike or no strike and remittance or no remittance. However, if you want to picket, take it completely away from the restricted areas. Moreover, the court had given an order. That is contempt of court, and it is a very serious thing. “The unions are saying that some airlines owe money. Are they the collecting agency? There are legal avenues through which the NCAA can recover its money. They can go to court and obtain judgments, after which court bailiffs can lawfully seize assets equivalent to the amount owed. There is also an allegation that Air Peace and some other airlines do not allow unions in their organisations. But being a member of a union is voluntary.” Airline’s position Meanwhile, Air Peace’s Chief Operating Officer, Mrs Oluwatoyin Olajide, warned that if affected passengers seek compensation over the disruption, the unions responsible for the picketing should be held liable for the consequences of their actions. The post Outrage grows as stakeholders raise airport security, safety concerns over picketing of Air Peace appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: S’Korea president proposes talks with North to formally end Korean War
items.description: South Korean President Lee Jae Myung proposed talks with North Korea to formally end the long-running Korean War, as Pyongyang deepens ties with Russia while asserting its status as an “irreversible” nuclear state. The two Koreas remain technically at war because their 1950-53 conflict, triggered by a North Korean attack, ended with an armistice rather than a peace treaty. Lee made the proposal in his speech at a ceremony marking the anniversary of Korea’s liberation from Japan’s 1910-45 colonial rule. “Let us put down our intentions to threaten each other and begin discussions to end the long-running war as the directly involved parties,” Lee said in his speech. “Through this, it may also be possible to discuss effective measures to halt the advancement of North Korea’s nuclear capabilities,” he added. Lee’s proposal came as North Korea this week denounced upcoming annual US-South Korean military drills, warning of stronger deterrence measures. Pyongyang has also recently been bristling over Japan’s gradual military build-up in the Pacific — firing off two missiles in as many weeks after Tokyo pledged to up its defence capabilities with a “sense of urgency and crisis”. North Korea has repeatedly declared itself an “irreversible” nuclear state since a 2019 summit between Kim and US counterpart Donald Trump in Hanoi collapsed over the scope of denuclearisation and sanctions relief. South Korea’s dovish President Lee has reversed the stance of his hawkish predecessor since taking power in Seoul in June 2025, offering nuclear-armed Pyongyang talks without preconditions. In July, South Korea’s unification minister even claimed Seoul had abandoned its campaign prioritising pressure on the North to dismantle its nuclear weapons, focusing instead on halting the expansion of Pyongyang’s nuclear activities. The hermetic leadership of North Korea has yet to respond to Lee’s repeated offers, and has instead bolstered military ties with Russia. Analysts say Pyongyang is receiving financial support, food, energy and military technology from Moscow for supplying troops and munitions for Russia’s war in Ukraine. North Korean leader Kim Jong Un is expected to visit Russia later this year, potentially to discuss further weapons supplies to Moscow. Washington, Seoul’s key security ally, stations about 28,500 troops in South Korea to bolter the country’s defences against military threats from Pyongyang. Colonel Ryan Donald, spokesman for the US and South Korean Combined Forces Command, said this week that North Korea’s deployment to the European war had changed the threat his soldiers may face on the Korean peninsula. “They’ve taken those lessons they learned there and brought them back to North Korea,” he told reporters as he talked about the 11-day South Korea-US joint exercises due to begin Monday. “Our training accounts for that threat.” AFP The post S’Korea president proposes talks with North to formally end Korean War appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: 2km of Chaos: How Asaba-Onitsha Expressway punishes road users, businesses
items.description: By Egufe Yafugborhi FOR motorists travelling from Benin through Asaba to Onitsha, the journey is increasingly becoming a test of patience, vehicle endurance and sheer determination. The ordeal reaches a painful climax on the roughly two-kilometre stretch from Okwe Junction to the New Building Materials Market. The section of the Asaba-Onitsha Expressway has deteriorated into a chaotic corridor of collapsed road portions, muddy shoulders, stagnant water and shattered motorable lanes, forcing cars, buses and heavy-duty trucks into desperate battle for space. This situation is particularly severe after the Koka Flyover, where the contractor handling major repairs has concentrated work on the right lane towards Onitsha, leaving the opposite lane badly damaged. Motorists say the apparent absence of workers on the site for weeks has worsened the situation. “So often, when heavy trucks and large buses jam the only motorable lane to and fro, you have a chaos, almost every hour of the day,” a minibus driver, Lucky Benson, told Vanguard. He said businesses, including hotels and car wash operators along the affected side, had withered as motorists increasingly avoided the area. The chaos compounds the hardship already experienced by travellers along the Benin-Asaba corridor. Ifeanyi Anthony, a Delta civil servant from Agbor who works in Asaba, said commuters spend hours negotiating failed portions of the highway. “Last week on our coming to Agbor from Asaba, we spent over two hours just to pass through Ubulu-Okiti. We also got stuck at Igbodo, Ogwashi-Uku junction,” he said. According to him, motorists now divert through Olona-Iselu and Iselu-Uku to escape collapsed sections, putting additional pressure on the adjoining roads. The uncompleted Okpanam bypass, expected to link the Second Niger Bridge and ease pressure on the main expressway, has further compounded the traffic burden. For motorists, traders and commuters, the two-kilometre stretch has become more than a bad road—it is a daily economic and human ordeal. The post 2km of Chaos: How Asaba-Onitsha Expressway punishes road users, businesses appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: More knocks on Kano mass wedding: ‘Same compassion should go to schools, hospitals’
items.description: By Juliet Umeh The wedding bells have gone silent in Kano. The colourful outfits have been put away, the rice served, prayers offered and the 1,500 couples who participated in the Kano State Government-sponsored mass wedding have begun what may be the most difficult part of the entire exercise – marriage itself. For the newlyweds, the real ceremony begins after the celebration. It begins with rent, food, electricity, healthcare, transportation, employment and, eventually, the cost of raising children. That reality has transformed Kano’s mass wedding programme from a celebration of matrimony into a debate about poverty, governance and government priorities. The state government reportedly committed about N1.5 billion to the exercise. Each bride received N100,000 as dowry, with another N100,000 reportedly provided as capital support, alongside household items including beds, bags of rice and cooking utensils. While the government says the programme is designed to help economically disadvantaged people overcome the financial barriers of marriage, critics are asking a fundamental question: Is helping poor people get married enough when the economic conditions that made marriage difficult remain unchanged? Reacting to the development on Arise TV’s What’s Trending, broadcaster Ayo Mairo-Eese questioned how the programme should be measured. “It is funny but not funny. It is just that you have no choice but to laugh at some of these things. Is this development?” she asked. According to her, government interventions should be measured by outcomes rather than the number of items distributed. “How do you measure success? These are the things developmental organizations will use as metrics to determine whether or not what they are doing is working,” she said. A bed is useful. A bag of rice is useful. Cooking utensils are useful. But none provides sustainable income, creates employment, repairs roads, provides electricity or keeps children in school. What happens after the wedding? Dr Ruben Abati, who also participated in the discussion, questioned whether the programme was a case of misplaced priorities. “The mass wedding, we were told, cost the state government about N1.5 billion. N100,000 given to each bride as dowry, another N100,000 given as a capital grant,” he said. Abati also raised concerns about population growth and family planning, arguing that the government appeared to be deliberately encouraging population increase. “And so that the couple don’t go hungry, they have been given a bag of rice each,” he said sarcastically. His larger concern, however, was sustainability. The success of the programme, he suggested, should not simply be measured by the number of couples brought together, but whether those marriages can survive the economic pressures ahead. Rufai Oseni, another presenter, brought electricity into the debate. “I want to make a vital point. One thing I see missing here are generators or solar,” he said. Behind the humour was a serious point: newly married couples need more than household items to run their homes. Government should not stop at the wedding For Public Relations and Communications Strategist, Mr Barnabas Akindele, the mass wedding should not be dismissed entirely. He described it as “a commendable display of benevolence”, particularly at a time when the cost of marriage has become burdensome. But he said government support should not end with the ceremony. “Such generosity should not end with weddings. The same compassion and resources directed towards helping people establish homes should also be extended to education, healthcare and the general welfare of citizens,” he said. Akindele added: “Government should be judged not only by the ceremonies it facilitates, but also by the quality of life it creates.” ‘It is a misplaced priority’ Alhaja Bunmi Yekini, who spoke to Saturday Vanguard, was more critical. She described the programme as a “misplaced priority”, arguing that Kano has more pressing challenges. “Kano State is one of the poorest states when it comes to the poverty index in Nigeria,” she said. “These are things that a state like Kano should focus on, not spending millions, billions rather, on weddings, mass weddings,” she added. Yekini said government should focus more on jobs, education and getting people out of poverty. “You are not employing people. You are not educating people. The next thing you think is best for the people of the state is to conduct a mass wedding with taxpayers’ money,” she said. She also expressed concern over reports involving a 17-year-old bride, questioning what life skills and opportunities would be available to young people entering marriage at such an age. ‘Empower them to pay for their weddings’ Media and Communications Officer, CAPPA, Mr Robert Egbe, acknowledged that the state was responding to a genuine social need but questioned whether the N1.5 billion could have produced greater impact through economic empowerment. “The Kano State Government says mass weddings are a way to help economically vulnerable intending couples begin married life with economic and household support. So you can see that they believe that it is an important societal need,” he said. However, Egbe noted that N1.5 billion for 1,500 couples translates to about N1 million per couple. “I’m wondering if it would not have been better to use the N1.5bn to economically empower economically challenged residents so they can make enough money to pay for their own weddings,” he said. The post More knocks on Kano mass wedding: ‘Same compassion should go to schools, hospitals’ appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Quand les Tunisiennes réécrivent Beauvoir
items.description: Le 13 août 2026, la Tunisie a célébré les 70 ans du Code du statut personnel, promulgué le 13 août 1956, quelques mois après l’indépendance et près d’un an avant la proclamation de la République. Tout a été dit sur le caractère exceptionnel de ce texte et sur l’audace de Bourguiba, qui s’est attaqué à des règles que l’on croyait intangibles. Mais cette année, quelque chose trouble la célébration. Monia Kallel * Jamais peut-être la fête du 13-Août n’aura suscité autant de controverses. La femme tunisienne est à nouveau sommée de se justifier : sur ses acquis, ses vêtements, son corps. Les gardiens de la morale, de plus en plus décomplexés, ne se contentent plus de regarder : ils prescrivent. Dans le même temps, les voix qui réclament une révision du CSP se font plus audibles, et de plus en plus radicales. Mais le plus inquiétant n’est peut-être pas que le CSP soit ouvertement remis en question. C’est que la contestation se déplace, gagne du terrain, change de visage — et qu’elle trouve parfois des alliées parmi celles-là mêmes qui ont bénéficié de ses avancées. Le corps féminin, territoire à surveiller Il y a d’abord cette campagne virulente autour des vêtements des femmes. Le corps féminin redevient un territoire à surveiller, à commenter, à corriger. On ne dit plus seulement à la femme ce qu’elle doit faire : on lui dit comment elle doit être vue. Le moralisme se mêle au prosélytisme. On le perçoit aussi dans ces voix qui réclament le retour à ce qui fut, en 1956, l’une des ruptures les plus audacieuses avec la tradition juridique : la polygamie. Celle-ci redevient un sujet de discussion ; même des députés s’en mêlent. Et puis il y a l’autre front, plus fort encore : celui qui conteste l’égalité dans l’héritage. Là, la situation devient presque vertigineuse. Car ce ne sont pas seulement les adversaires traditionnels des droits des femmes qui la contestent. De nombreux «modernistes» , hommes et femmes, s’opposent à cette revendication. Et lorsqu’une responsable féministe affirme que l’égalité dans l’héritage doit désormais être au cœur du combat, elle se retrouve au centre d’une cabale qui dépasse largement la discussion juridique. Voilà le paradoxe. Les femmes tunisiennes sont légitimement fières du CSP. Elles savent ce qu’il a changé dans leur vie et dans celle de leurs mères et de leurs grands-mères. Elles célèbrent l’audace de Bourguiba lorsqu’il a transgressé, interprété le texte, contextualisé, fait entrer le droit dans une société nouvelle. Mais lorsqu’il s'agit de l’héritage, lorsqu’il s’agit de franchir un pas de plus, certaines invoquent soudain la règle «claire et nette» du texte religieux. Comme si l’histoire, l’évolution, le temps devaient s’arrêter exactement là où commencent nos hésitations et nos craintes. Comme si la famille tunisienne de 2026 était encore celle de 1956. Elle ne l’est évidemment plus. La structure de la famille a changé. Le rôle économique des femmes a changé. Leur niveau d’instruction, leur accès au travail, leur contribution aux revenus familiaux, leur espérance de vie, leur place dans l’espace public ont changé. La société elle-même a changé. Pourquoi donc l’histoire serait-elle convoquée pour justifier certaines transgressions et congédiée lorsqu’il faudrait en accomplir une nouvelle ? C’est peut-être là le paradoxe le plus profond de notre rapport aux droits des femmes. Nous aimons les droits lorsqu’ils nous arrivent sur un plateau d’argent. Nous les célébrons lorsqu’un État les inscrit dans la loi. Nous sommes fières lorsque l’histoire nous les offre. Mais sommes-nous prêtes à nous battre pour ceux qui ne sont pas encore acquis ? C’est une autre affaire. 70 ans après | Le combat recommencé pour les droits des femmes en Tunisie Des droits jamais vraiment acquis En 1949, Simone de Beauvoir écrivait : «N’oubliez jamais qu’il suffira d’une crise politique, économique ou religieuse pour que les droits des femmes soient remis en question. Ces droits ne sont jamais acquis.» La Tunisie pourrait ajouter aujourd’hui quelque chose à cette phrase. Les droits des femmes sont d’autant plus fragiles lorsqu’ils ont été accordés par un pouvoir qui, même lorsqu’il se voulait progressiste, demeurait un pouvoir masculin. Le CSP est l’une des grandes réussites de ce que l’on a appelé le féminisme d’État. Mais le féminisme d’État comporte une ambiguïté fondamentale : il peut faire gagner aux femmes plusieurs décennies en quelques années, mais il ne leur apprend pas nécessairement à devenir les sujets politiques de leurs propres droits. Le CSP de 1956 n’est pas le produit d’une évolution spontanée de la société tunisienne : il est le résultat d’une volonté politique extraordinairement forte. Bourguiba a assumé une lecture politique et réformatrice de l’islam. Et nous continuons à en parler comme si le zaïm était encore là. C’est peut-être notre problème. Le «sauveur» est une figure tenace. Chez les conservateurs, il prend parfois la forme du religieux qui vient expliquer aux femmes comment être de bonnes musulmanes. Chez les modernistes, il peut prendre celle du dirigeant éclairé qui vient expliquer aux femmes comment être libres. Dans les deux cas, le mécanisme est étrangement proche. Bourguiba est justement célébré parce qu’il a osé. Mais qui, après Bourguiba, osera ? Et surtout : pourquoi faudrait-il encore attendre qu’un homme ose à notre place ? C’est ici que la réflexion de Simone de Beauvoir, si précieuse, paraît à la fois prophétique et incomplète. Il ne suffit pas de rester vigilantes. Il faut devenir actrices de la construction, de la défense et de l’extension de nos droits. Car un droit que personne ne porte politiquement devient rapidement un droit que d’autres peuvent redéfinir. Et un droit dont les principales bénéficiaires ne se sentent pas responsables peut finir par paraître étranger à celles-là mêmes qu’il protège. Que sommes-nous prêtes à conquérir ? Voilà pourquoi la bataille actuelle ne se résume pas au CSP. Le CSP traversera probablement cette tempête. Il a traversé bien d’autres vents contraires. Et l’égalité successorale finira, tôt ou tard, par devenir une réalité, parce que les sociétés changent, parce que les familles changent, parce que les femmes changent, et parce que le droit ne peut indéfiniment prétendre que le monde est demeuré celui d’hier. La vraie question est ailleurs. Sommes-nous capables de défendre ce que nous avons reçu et de conquérir ce que nous n’avons pas encore reçu ? Sommes-nous capables de passer du statut de bénéficiaires à celui de citoyennes qui savent que les droits ne sont pas des cadeaux ? Le 13 août ne devrait donc pas être seulement la fête d’une femme à qui l’État a donné des droits. Il devrait être le jour où les Tunisiennes se demandent ce qu’elles sont prêtes à faire pour que ces droits deviennent réellement les leurs. Car il existe une autre manière de perdre ses droits que de les voir supprimer par une loi. C’est de renoncer à les défendre. Ennahdha peut renaître de plusieurs manières. Ce parti conservateur peut renaître d’une crise politique, d’une crise économique, d’une poussée religieuse. Mais il peut aussi renaître d’une abdication beaucoup plus silencieuse : celle des femmes elles-mêmes. Après le 13 août, la question n’est plus seulement : que nous a-t-on donné ? Mais : que sommes-nous prêtes à défendre et à conquérir ? * Ecrivaine. Tunisie | Le combat pour l’égalité en matière d’héritage se poursuit L’article Quand les Tunisiennes réécrivent Beauvoir est apparu en premier sur Kapitalis .

items.title: Soldiers trying to prevent my entry into Osun, Davido alleges
items.description: Afrobeats superstar David Adeleke, popularly known as Davido, has alleged that soldiers are attempting to prevent him from entering Osun State as residents prepare to vote in Saturday’s governorship election. Davido made the claim in a post on his verified X account early Saturday, saying he had been informed that soldiers were seeking to stop him from gaining access to the state. “I’ve been reliably informed that soldiers are trying to prevent me from entering Osun tomorrow, this won’t happen, every citizen of Nigeria has the right to movement at any point of time,” he wrote. The allegation came hours after the Nigeria Police Force announced a restriction of movement across Osun State as part of security measures for the election. According to the police, the restriction took effect from 12:00 midnight on Friday, August 14, and will remain in place until 6:00 p.m. on Saturday, August 15, 2026. Thousands of police officers and other security personnel have been deployed across the state to maintain law and order during the governorship poll. Davido, who is a nephew of incumbent Governor Ademola Adeleke, has played an active role in his uncle’s re-election campaign under the Accord Party. Governor Adeleke is seeking a second term and faces opposition from candidates including the All Progressives Congress candidate, Bola Oyebamiji, among others. The singer’s allegation generated significant reactions online, with some users arguing that the reported attempt to restrict his movement could be connected to the general election-day security measures. Others, however, raised concerns over the possibility of security agencies imposing targeted restrictions on the high-profile supporter of the incumbent governor. Reacting to Davido’s post, former presidential media aide Bashir Ahmad described the singer’s claim as “dramatic”, arguing that movement restrictions had already been announced as part of the security arrangements for the election. “You are just dramatic, @davido. It has been widely announced by the security operators that movement in and around Osun will be restricted from 12 midnight today until 6 pm today due to the election and this is a standard security measure during elections anywhere not peculiar to Osun. “So the right to freedom of movement does not mean ignoring lawful security measures put in place to ensure a peaceful and credible election,” Ahmad wrote. The post Soldiers trying to prevent my entry into Osun, Davido alleges appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: The Door Must Stay Open: What women in Nigerian universities have learned to fear, by Stephanie Shaakaa
items.description: The silence of the ivory tower has a particular sound. I have learned to recognize it in the hesitant knock on my office door. A student stands there holding a project file, starting with a question about a grade or a deadline. Then she sits down, looks at me, and the academic question gives way to something else: a lecturer who made her uncomfortable; a supervisor asking to see her after hours, or a hint that her academic future depends on becoming more accommodating. Sometimes she says all of this. Sometimes she only says, “Ma, I have a problem.” By then, you know the problem is larger than her words. This is one of the least discussed consequences of corruption in our universities. We treat sexual harassment, coercion, and academic exploitation as the isolated failures of a few morally bankrupt individuals. We identify the guilty lecturer, the harmed student, and the administrator who mishandled the complaint, and then we move on. But systems are defined just as much by what happens around the misconduct: who is believed, whose reputation is protected, and how much courage it takes to tell the truth. That is where the deeper damage begins. Corruption changes the behavior of people who have never participated in it, particularly women. There is a deliberate distance female lecturers often maintain. From the outside, it looks like arrogance or formality. A student might wonder why a pleasant departmental colleague becomes so careful behind closed doors. The answer is not a lack of care; it is the exact opposite. I keep my office door open. It is a small thing, but vital for professional survival. The corridor light remains visible. Passersby can see who is inside. A private conversation remains, to some extent, public. The open door is not hostility, it is a boundary. So is refusing to meet students alone late at night, keeping communication strictly professional, and avoiding casual familiarity that can be distorted. These precautions can make a woman appear distant. Sometimes, distance is simply the price of safety. This is hard to explain to those who never have to weigh how their ordinary behavior might be weaponized. A male lecturer can be informal and be seen as approachable; a female lecturer doing the same risks having her warmth misinterpreted. A strict man is disciplined; a strict man’s female counterpart is difficult. A distant man is authoritative; a distant man’s female counterpart is proud. Women enter these interactions with an exhausting, constant awareness of how easily their conduct can be twisted. They learn to calculate things that should never require calculation: How late is too late? How familiar is too familiar? Should I close the door? At some point, professionalism stops being just a standard of conduct and becomes defensive architecture. Corruption teaches innocent people to behave as though danger is always nearby. Then comes the cruelest irony. The women most careful about boundaries become the safe havens that vulnerable students seek out. A student facing an inappropriate encounter may pass several offices before knocking on a woman’s door. She may not know her well, but she hopes for a conversation that will not immediately turn into a negotiation. She needs someone to listen without first asking what she did to cause the problem. And so the woman who spent years building careful professional boundaries becomes the emergency room for the institution’s wounded. This uncounted burden exists entirely outside the ordinary demands of teaching, research, and administration. There is no promotion point for helping a student regain confidence after an authority figure has abused their power. Yet women perform this work anyway, acting as unofficial counselors, procedure interpreters, and the last bridge between a frightened student and a broken institution. This is why academic corruption changes the entire atmosphere. Students grow suspicious, lecturers become guarded, and women navigate ordinary interactions with extreme caution. Trust fractures. People develop private systems of protection. Women keep doors open; students study which lecturers to avoid. None of this appears in a university prospectus, but everyone learns it fast. That proves why the “few bad apples” argument fails. The institution must examine the conditions allowing such behavior to survive, the systems discouraging complaints, and a culture that prioritizes public relations over human safety. Telling women to be more careful is useless; they are already exhausting themselves with caution. Telling students to speak up means nothing while the costs of speaking out remain devastating. Universities need credible reportage channels, transparent supervisory relationships, and accountability that never shields institutional failure. Academic authority is a trust meant for guiding another human being. A lecturer does not own a student’s future. A supervisor does not own a degree. The moment authority becomes a bargaining chip, education is corrupted. That is why I keep my door open. Not out of coldness, but to keep boundaries clear so neither of us has to guess what the relationship means. I want the corridor visible. I want the student sitting across from me to know that help does not come with a hidden price. Yet it is deeply basic that any of this is necessary. A university should not force decent people behind defensive walls. A woman should not have to calculate the warmth of her own voice to remain above suspicion. The shame belongs entirely to an academic culture that makes good people afraid to be ordinary. Because the deepest damage of corruption is not just a lost grade or a compromised degree it is that a place built to teach trust becomes a place where everyone learns to defend themselves against it.
